# **Agro–Ecological Zoning**

2026 | 10 | 07 Last compiled: `r Sys.Date()`

The Agro–Ecological Zoning (AEZ) methodology is based on the principles of land evaluation (FAO, 1976), and it serves as a framework supporting sustainable agricultural development by delineating various agricultural land utilization possibilities. 

# **Multi-criteria decision analysis**

2026 | 10 | 09 Last compiled: `r Sys.Date()`

There is a review paper about agrivoltaic spatial suitability [Geospatial planning strategies for agrivoltaic systems: a review of criteria, decision models and emerging challenges](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2213138825002759).

Khazael et al. (2025) reported *The findings indicate that most spatial studies on AVS have been concentrated in the Northern Hemisphere and have predominantly relied on traditional multi-criteria decision-making models, with a notable absence of AI-driven planning solutions. Furthermore, much of the research overlooks comprehensive spatial evidence, particularly those related to soil characteristics and water availability.*

![Figure: Geospatial planning workflow](images/geospatial_planning.png){width=75% fig-align="center"}

Criteria need to be considered in the AV spatial planning: **climate, geographical criteria, infrastructure, exclusion**. 

**1. Climate**: Solar radiation, temperature, precipitation, cloud and shade intensity, wind speed

![Figure: Climate criteria](images/climate_criteria.png){width=100% fig-align="center"}

**2. Geographical criteria**: Slope, aspect, LULC, cropland extent

![Figure: Geographical criteria](images/geo_criteria.png){width=50% fig-align="center"}


**3. Infrastructure criteria**: Proximity to power grid, proximity to road, proximity to settlement

![Figure: Infrastructure criteria](images/infra_criteria.png){width=50% fig-align="center"}


**4. Exclusionary criteria**: Protected area

![Figure: Exclusionary criteria](images/exclusion_criteria.png){width=100% fig-align="center"}


Some factors may important but not considered in most literature

![Figure: Absent factors](images/absent_factors.png){width=100% fig-align="center"}
